mood.p: De laatste dag van de meteorologische zomer voelt eerder als herfst. Het is sterk wisselvallig met maar af en toe zon, verspreide buien en kans op onweer, kleine hagel en windstoten tot 75 kilometer per uur. Vooral in het noordwesten kan lokaal veel neerslag vallen, tot zo'n 60 millimeter, bij een maximum van ongeveer 20 graden en een matige tot krachtige zuidwestenwind. Politiek is de spanning minstens zo groot: de coalitie onderhandelde de hele nacht door over de begroting zonder akkoord, terwijl Amsterdam bijkomt van de steekpartij op Centraal en in Groningen een hoogspanningsstation nog dagen zal branden.

global.h3: US strikes Iranian launchers on Larak Island
global.summary: American forces hit Revolutionary Guard positions on Larak Island, the first US attack on Iranian targets in weeks.
body: US forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island near the Strait of Hormuz, ending a lull of several weeks in direct attacks. Washington said Revolutionary Guard units had been observed preparing to fire rockets carrying sea mines into the shipping lane.

The strait remains the flashpoint of the wider conflict. Iran has claimed control over the waterway and roughly 400 vessels with about 6,000 crew are still stuck inside the Persian Gulf, according to the International Maritime Organization.
The disruption is feeding through to fuel markets and has pushed pump prices higher in the United States, adding domestic political pressure to an already volatile military standoff.

global.h3: 400 ships still trapped in the Persian Gulf
global.summary: Roughly 6,000 crew remain stranded aboard vessels unable to leave the Gulf as Iran asserts control over the Strait of Hormuz.
body: The International Maritime Organization says around 400 ships are still unable to transit the Strait of Hormuz, leaving about 6,000 seafarers stuck on board. Iran has publicly claimed control over the waterway.
The blockade has become one of the most consequential economic effects of the conflict, choking a route that normally carries a large share of the world's seaborne crude and refined products.
Shipowners face mounting insurance costs and crews are facing extended stays at sea with no clear timetable for release.

global.h3: 37 dead in Russian airstrike on Ukraine
global.summary: At least 37 people were killed and dozens injured when a Russian strike triggered a large secondary explosion.
body: Ukrainian authorities reported at least 37 dead and dozens wounded after a Russian air attack on a building that appears to have contained explosives. The secondary blast greatly amplified the damage.
The strike came during a renewed round of long range exchanges. Ukraine is reported to have hit an oil refinery deep inside Russia while Russian drones targeted Kyiv.
Casualty figures were still being revised as rescue teams worked through the debris.

global.h3: IAEA reports drone attacks near Zaporizhzhia plant
global.summary: The UN nuclear watchdog says drones struck close to Europe's largest nuclear power station and urged both sides to hold back.
body: The International Atomic Energy Agency confirmed drone attacks in the immediate area of the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant. Agency chief Rafael Grossi called on Russia and Ukraine to exercise restraint around the site.

The plant has repeatedly been caught in the fighting since the start of the war and inspectors have warned that repeated strikes near cooling and power infrastructure raise the risk of a serious incident.
No radiological release was reported.

global.h3: Mutinying soldiers spark explosions in Niger capital
global.summary: Fighting broke out around Niamey including near the international airport as mutinous troops moved against the government.
body: Explosions and gunfire were reported across Niamey as mutinying soldiers clashed with loyalist forces. Some of the fighting took place near the city's international airport.
Niger has been under military rule since the 2023 coup and the latest unrest points to fractures within the security apparatus that installed the current leadership.
The situation remained unclear with communications disrupted and no immediate confirmation of who controls key installations.

global.h3: Israeli settlers attack West Bank village
global.summary: Palestinians were injured when settlers raided a West Bank village, and an NBC News crew was reportedly assaulted in a separate incident.
body: Israeli settlers attacked a village in the occupied West Bank, wounding Palestinians before the army removed them from a house and the surrounding area. Vehicles used in the raid were seized and troops remained nearby.
In a separate reported incident, a Palestinian woman and an NBC News team were attacked while working in the territory.
Settler violence has climbed sharply over the past two years and rights groups say prosecutions remain rare.

global.h3: Israeli strike kills 3-year-old child in Gaza
global.summary: A young child was killed in an Israeli strike in Gaza as aid groups renewed calls for accountability over earlier attacks.
body: Al Jazeera reported that a 3-year-old child was killed in an Israeli strike in Gaza, one of a continuing series of casualties among the youngest of the territory's population.
Separately, chef Jose Andres renewed his call for a full investigation into the killing of World Central Kitchen staff in Gaza, saying the case remains unresolved.
Humanitarian access into the territory remains heavily constrained.

global.h3: Zambia opposition leader charged with treason
global.summary: Brian Mundubile and his running mate Makebi Zulu have been charged with treason ahead of a contested political season.
body: Zambian opposition leader Brian Mundubile and his running mate Makebi Zulu were charged with treason, a capital offence under Zambian law.
The charges land in the middle of an increasingly tense political period and opposition figures argue the case is designed to remove a credible challenger from the field.
Prosecutors have not made the full evidentiary basis public.

global.h3: US pushes 18-nation anti-cartel military coalition
global.summary: Washington wants a coalition with 18 Latin American countries to run joint military operations against drug cartels.
body: The United States is proposing an anti-cartel coalition bringing together 18 Latin American countries for coordinated military operations against trafficking networks.
The plan represents a significant escalation of the militarised approach to narcotics and raises sovereignty questions for participating governments.
Details on command structures, rules of engagement and funding have not been released.

global.h3: Iceland votes 52.8% against reopening EU talks
global.summary: Icelanders narrowly rejected restarting accession negotiations with the European Union after a bitter campaign.
body: Iceland voted against resuming European Union accession talks, with 52.8 percent opposed and 47.2 percent in favour according to public broadcaster RUV. Turnout and regional splits shaped a very tight result.
The sitting government had pushed to restart the process it froze years ago, arguing that geopolitical instability made closer European integration more attractive.
The outcome closes off the accession route for the current parliamentary term and hands a win to the fisheries and sovereignty campaigners who dominated the no side.

global.h3: Rival Libyan factions agree elections within two years
global.summary: A deal signed at the UN mission in Tripoli commits Libya's competing power centres to national elections inside two years.
body: Libya's rival factions signed an agreement at the United Nations mission in Tripoli committing to hold national elections within two years. An initial draft was produced by a UN backed committee meeting in Tunis on 20 August.
Libya has not held a successful national vote since the postponed 2021 presidential election and remains split between rival administrations in the west and east.
Previous timetables have slipped repeatedly, so implementation rather than signature will determine whether this round is different.

global.h3: Syria reopens its embassy in Libya
global.summary: Damascus is restoring diplomatic representation in Tripoli after talks between the two foreign ministries.
body: Syria will reopen its embassy in Libya following talks in Tripoli between Syria's interim foreign minister Asaad Shaibani and Libyan counterpart Taher al-Baour.
The move is part of a broader push by Syria's post-Assad leadership to rebuild diplomatic ties across the Arab world and normalise its international position.
Officials framed the reopening as the start of a new phase in relations between the two states.

global.h3: Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan to meet in Istanbul
global.summary: Foreign and defence ministers plus military chiefs from the three states gather for the first time since signing the Mecca pact.
body: Senior officials from Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan will meet in Istanbul, their first joint gathering since the three signed the Mecca pact. Foreign ministers, defence ministers and military chiefs are all expected.
The alignment links a NATO member, the Gulf's largest economy and a nuclear armed South Asian state, and is being watched closely by regional rivals.
The agenda is expected to cover defence coordination and the wider fallout from the conflict with Iran.

global.h3: Venezuela defends oil deal handing US 65bn barrels
global.summary: Delcy Rodriguez says the agreement with Trump brings endless benefits as critics call it a giveaway of national resources.
body: Venezuelan vice president Delcy Rodriguez publicly defended the oil agreement struck with Donald Trump, describing the benefits for Venezuela as endless. Trump has said the United States gains control over more than 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan reserves.
Trump is under domestic pressure over petrol prices that have risen sharply since the war with Iran began, and the deal is being sold at home as a supply fix.
The Venezuelan opposition has objected strongly to reports that Washington sought a large stake in the country's oil and gas sector.

global.h3: Canada erects giant Lake Ontario sign in Trump spat
global.summary: Ontario's premier unveiled a defiant sign after Trump ordered the lake renamed Lake America and Google Maps followed suit.
body: Ontario premier Doug Ford unveiled a large sign reading Lake Ontario, Now and Always at a conservation area near Grimsby, a direct answer to Trump's executive order renaming the lake as Lake America. Trump then posted video of himself kicking over a Lake Ontario sign.
Google Maps has adopted the new name for United States users while keeping Lake Ontario for Canadian users, saying it follows the naming decision of the relevant US government agency.
The row is the latest flashpoint in a deteriorating relationship between Washington and Ottawa.

global.h3: Pacific Islands Forum in turmoil as leaders pull out
global.summary: Several heads of government withdrew from the 55th leaders meeting in Palau, throwing the summit into disarray.
body: The 55th Pacific Islands Forum Leaders Meeting in Palau was thrown into confusion after several leaders pulled out, undercutting the region's main political gathering.
The forum has been strained by competition between the United States, Australia and China for influence across the Pacific, and by disputes over membership and agenda setting.
Delegates had already arrived in Koror when the withdrawals became clear.

global.h3: Fed chair signals rate rises are back on the table
global.summary: The US central bank chief voiced concern about inflation while keeping options open on the next policy move.
body: The chair of the US Federal Reserve expressed concern about the inflation outlook and declined to rule out interest rate increases in the coming months.
Energy costs driven by the Gulf conflict are the main new pressure, feeding into transport and production prices across the economy.
Markets had been positioned for a steady or easing path, so the shift in tone matters for borrowing costs well beyond the United States.

global.h3: Spain asks Frontex for help with migrants in Ceuta
global.summary: Thousands of migrants remain in the Spanish enclave a month after tens of thousands stormed the border.
body: Spain has requested assistance from the European border agency Frontex to manage the situation in Ceuta. Thousands of people remain in the North African enclave without legal status after last month's mass crossing.
The July surge saw tens of thousands attempt to enter at once, overwhelming local reception capacity in a territory of limited size.
The request pulls the European Union directly into a situation Madrid has so far handled largely on its own.

global.h3: 804 dead and 3,000 missing in Nepal-Tibet floods
global.summary: The confirmed toll from the Himalayan glacier collapse keeps climbing as rescuers race to free workers trapped in a tunnel.
body: The death toll from the flash floods triggered by a Himalayan glacier collapse has reached 804, with 788 bodies recovered in Nepal and 16 in Tibet. More than 3,000 people are still missing across the disaster zone.

Rescue teams are working to reach workers trapped in a flooded tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydropower project in Rasuwa district, while fresh flooding alerts have been issued on both sides of the border. The Red Cross estimates at least 93,000 people are in great need.
Foreign nationals are among the missing, including 261 people unaccounted for on the Chinese side, and mass burials have begun in Chitwan district as morgues fill.

global.h3: Ferry captain arrested after 8 die off northern Cyprus
global.summary: A passenger vessel capsized shortly after leaving Girne, killing at least eight people with 18 still missing.
body: A ferry capsized off the coast of northern Cyprus shortly after departing the port of Girne, killing at least eight people. An estimated 237 passengers were rescued and 18 remained missing.
The captain and crew have been arrested. A witness on board said crew members fled the vessel before passengers had been brought to safety.
The cause of the capsizing has not been established.

global.h3: Sudan war refugees face dire conditions in El Obeid
global.summary: Civilians fleeing the civil war are arriving daily at a shockingly overcrowded refuge city with collapsing services.
body: Aid workers describe conditions in El Obeid and the camps on its outskirts as dire and deteriorating, with traumatised civilians arriving every day from the front lines of Sudan's civil war.
The city has become a primary refuge point but shelter, water and medical capacity are far below what the caseload requires.
Sudan's conflict remains one of the largest displacement crises in the world and continues to receive a fraction of the funding requested by relief agencies.

global.h3: UN says 200,000 forced back into gang-ruled Haiti
global.summary: Deportations to Haiti keep rising even as the UN records more than 1,400 killings in a single quarter.
body: The United Nations says 200,000 people have been forcibly returned to Haiti, a country where armed gangs control large parts of the territory. Deportation numbers have continued to rise.
Between April and June 2026 alone the UN registered 1,408 deaths and 656 injuries linked to the violence.
Returnees are being sent into areas where state authority is minimal and humanitarian access is severely restricted.

global.h3: Floodwaters sweep away lorry in the Philippines
global.summary: Video from the Philippines shows a heavy goods vehicle carried off by raging floodwater during severe seasonal flooding.
body: Footage circulating from the Philippines shows a lorry being swept away by fast moving floodwater, a stark illustration of the force of the current flooding.
The country is in the middle of its wet season and repeated storm systems have overwhelmed drainage and river defences in several provinces.
Authorities have been issuing evacuation advisories in the worst affected areas.

global.h3: Storms leave trail of destruction across northern Italy
global.summary: Dozens were injured in Cremona and tens of thousands of vehicles were damaged by severe weather.
body: Violent storms tore through northern Italy, injuring dozens of people in Cremona and damaging tens of thousands of cars along with homes and other buildings.
Hail and high winds accounted for most of the vehicle damage, and insurers face a large claims volume across the affected provinces.
The event adds to a summer of destructive convective storms across the Po valley.

netherlands.h3: Coalition still has no budget deal as deadline bites
netherlands.summary: Talks at the finance ministry ran through the night with no agreement, days before the Prinsjesdag deadline.
body: Coalition parties spent a full day negotiating at the ministry of finance without reaching a budget agreement, and talks continued overnight. The minority cabinet has to settle its internal differences after weeks of separate conversations with opposition parties.
The government lacks a majority and needs opposition votes to get its plans through parliament. D66, VVD and CDA are reported to disagree over what to concede to Pro on social security cuts.
The Prinsjesdag deadline leaves very little room to manoeuvre, and a failure to land a package would turn a budget dispute into a political crisis.

netherlands.h3: Klaver warns coalition it is manufacturing a crisis
netherlands.summary: The Pro leader says the planned social security cuts must go and accuses D66, VVD and CDA of driving toward breakdown.
body: Pro leader Jesse Klaver told D66, VVD and CDA that they are turning the budget standoff into a crisis and insisted his party must be listened to. He wants the planned cuts to social security withdrawn entirely.
Coalition parties are still weighing which opposition partner to build a majority with as the deadline approaches, and Pro's votes are one of the few available routes.
The dispute is as much about who gets credit and blame in the run up to the Senate elections as it is about the numbers.

netherlands.h3: AIVD and MIVD get broader powers, oversight trimmed
netherlands.summary: New rules let the intelligence services act faster without prior approval, citing threats from Russia, China and Iran.
body: The cabinet is expanding the powers of the AIVD and MIVD, allowing the services to intervene more easily without prior authorisation. Ministers point to intelligence threats from Russia, China and Iran as the justification.
The oversight body will continue to review activity, but experts warn that scaling back prior checks weakens the safeguards that made the Dutch system defensible.
Critics accept the law needed updating while arguing that modernisation does not require reducing supervision.

netherlands.h3: Cabinet apologises to 20,000 closed youth care survivors
netherlands.summary: The state, municipalities and the sector jointly apologised for abuse in closed youth care and freed up 12 million euros.
body: The cabinet, municipalities and the youth care sector issued a joint apology to more than 20,000 young people who were held in closed youth care institutions. A budget of 12 million euros has been set aside for recovery activities.
Mental health organisations say the apology is only a starting point and that the structural issues that produced the abuse have not been resolved.
Survivors have campaigned for years for recognition, compensation and an end to isolation practices in the sector.

netherlands.h3: Wind turbines must stand twice their blade height from homes
netherlands.summary: A 200 metre turbine will now need to be at least 400 metres from the nearest house under the new national standard.
body: The cabinet has set a national distance rule requiring wind turbines to be positioned at least twice their tip height away from homes. A turbine measuring 200 metres therefore needs 400 metres of clearance.
The standard ends years of legal uncertainty after courts struck down earlier national norms, but developers say it will shrink the number of viable onshore sites.
Separately the cabinet is trying to prevent further delays to offshore wind by restoring subsidies and opening talks with firms that took on contracts without them.

netherlands.h3: Cabinet weighs removing ON from the broadcasting system
netherlands.summary: A decision on the far-right broadcaster is due very soon after an item claiming Hitler was right.
body: Minister Letschert said a decision on whether the far-right broadcaster ON can be removed from the public broadcasting system will come very soon. The cabinet is examining the legal options.
The row was triggered by a programme item asserting that Hitler was right, and MPs have called for the show to be scrapped.
Removing a broadcaster from the system would be an exceptional step in a framework designed to protect pluralism.

netherlands.h3: TenneT substation fire in Groningen to burn for days
netherlands.summary: Six cellars each holding 140,000 litres of cooling oil are alight at the Meeden high-voltage station and cannot be doused with water.
body: A fire at the TenneT high-voltage substation in Meeden is expected to burn for several more days. The blaze is in six cellars each containing 140,000 litres of cooling oil.
Firefighters cannot use water because it would spread the burning oil, and the storage cellars are not safely accessible.
The site is a significant node in the northern grid and the outage risk is being watched closely as the fire continues.

netherlands.h3: Most student rooms are priced above the legal limit
netherlands.summary: A majority of student rooms breach the statutory rent cap while cities hand out almost no fines.
body: Research shows the majority of student rooms in the Netherlands are let at rents well above the legal maximum. Enforcement is close to non-existent in several of the biggest student cities.
Utrecht and Nijmegen issued no fines at all, and Amsterdam declined to share current figures with investigative programme Argos.
The findings land as students return for the new academic year into a rental market with almost no slack.

netherlands.h3: Dutch chip industry turnover doubles to 46bn euros
netherlands.summary: Semiconductor revenue in the Netherlands has doubled in six years, cementing the sector as a national economic anchor.
body: Turnover in the Dutch semiconductor industry has reached 46 billion euros, double the level of six years ago. The growth reflects sustained global demand for advanced lithography and chip equipment.
The cluster around Eindhoven and Veldhoven remains the centre of gravity, drawing suppliers, researchers and international staff.
The sector's weight also increases the country's exposure to export controls and geopolitical friction over chip technology.

netherlands.h3: Drought cuts harvests 10 to 30% but prices cushion farmers
netherlands.summary: Yields are well down after the driest spell in centuries, though higher market prices leave most growers roughly even.
body: Dutch harvests are coming in 10 to 30 percent below normal because of the prolonged drought. Higher prices for the reduced volumes mean the average farmer comes out reasonably well.
The dry summer has had wider effects on inland shipping, with the Twentekanaal only partially reopening after low water levels closed a lock since late July.
Conservationists report that the worst drought in 700 years has turned some wetland areas into fish kill zones.

netherlands.h3: 900 complaints filed over estate agents and unfair bidding
netherlands.summary: Homeowners association Vereniging Eigen Huis has logged more than 900 reports since reopening its complaints desk.
body: Vereniging Eigen Huis says it has received more than 900 reports since reopening its estate agent complaints desk, pointing to widespread problems with unfair bidding practices in the housing market.
Buyers describe closed bidding processes, shifting deadlines and offers that appear to be steered toward preferred parties.
The complaints add to pressure for tighter regulation of the brokerage sector in a market where buyers have almost no leverage.

netherlands.h3: 4 injured in Amsterdam Centraal stabbing streamed live
netherlands.summary: The attack at the north side of the station was broadcast on social media, and a suspect has been identified.
body: Four people were injured in a stabbing at the north side of Amsterdam Centraal station, reported at 19:30. One of the injured is the suspect, who has since been identified and arrested.
Parts of the incident were livestreamed on social media, which police are now using as evidence.
Investigators believe a fight preceded the stabbing.

netherlands.h3: Mass sperm donor says he has fathered 199 children
netherlands.summary: Donor Simon wrote to mothers claiming a far higher total than the 121 children reported this week, with another pregnancy under way.
body: Dutch mass sperm donor known as Simon has written to some of the mothers saying he has fathered 199 children, far above the 121 figure that emerged earlier in the week. One woman is currently pregnant.
UMC Groningen confirmed it had already reprimanded him years ago, raising questions about why the practice was allowed to continue.
Dutch guidelines cap a donor at a small number of families to limit the risk of unknowing consanguinity, and repeated breaches have exposed the weakness of enforcement.

netherlands.h3: August ranks as eighth warmest in Dutch records
netherlands.summary: The month closes as the eighth warmest August ever measured in the Netherlands.
body: This August will go into the books as the eighth warmest on the Dutch record, capping a summer marked by heat and an exceptional drought.
The warmth followed a season in which swimming spots and open water saw heavy use well into the late summer.
The meteorological summer ends on 31 August with a distinctly autumnal day of showers and wind.

netherlands.h3: Halsema says city liveability is buckling under strain
netherlands.summary: Amsterdam's mayor says homelessness and drug use in the big cities now require major intervention from The Hague.
body: Amsterdam mayor Femke Halsema warned that liveability in the big Dutch cities is under severe pressure from homelessness and drug use. She said the problems are gradually overwhelming municipal capacity.
Halsema argued that major measures from central government are needed to bring the nuisance down, framing it as beyond what individual cities can solve.
Her comments arrive as the cabinet is locked in budget talks with limited room for new spending commitments.

netherlands.h3: Dutch men's eight wins second straight rowing world title
netherlands.summary: The Holland Acht defended its world championship crown with a crew including Finn Florijn and Ralf Rienks.
body: The Dutch men's eight won the world championship title for the second year running. The crew included Ralf Rienks, Finn Florijn, Wibout Rustenburg, Jorn Salverda, Sander de Graaf, Pieter van Veen, Jan van der Bij and Mick Makker with cox Jonna de Vries.
The result confirms the boat as the benchmark in the event heading toward the next Olympic cycle.
It was a mixed sporting weekend for the Netherlands, with the women's hockey team losing the World Cup final to Argentina on a shoot-out.
